title: church words nobody defined
hook: quiet time, on fire, testimony: the church words you picked up like a family's inside jokes

segments.voice: Yesterday: baptism, under the water and up again. Today, the words people used around it, the ones nobody ever looked up.

Quiet time. On fire for God. A hedge of protection. Traveling mercies. If you grew up in church, you probably learned these the way you learn a family's inside jokes: by hearing them a lot. People even have a name for it: Christianese. Today, three of them, and what's actually behind them.

Quiet time means a few minutes alone each day to read the Bible and pray. It has a model. One Gospel says Jesus got up "a great while before day" and went off to a solitary place to pray. On fire means eager, all in. It echoes two friends on a road who said, after a stranger turned out to be Jesus, that their hearts had burned inside them while he talked. And testimony. At camp or youth group, someone stands by the bonfire and tells how they came to faith. Testimony is a courtroom word. In Greek it's martyria, from martys: a witness, someone who says what they saw. Early Christians who died rather than take back what they'd witnessed were called by that same word, and it came into English as martyr. So a testimony isn't a performance, and it isn't a sales pitch. It's a witness statement: here's what happened to me. Some people love telling theirs to a crowd. Plenty of Christians keep theirs for a friend, or for nobody but God.
screen: `QUIET TIME — A HABIT OF JESUS.` · `ON FIRE — A BURNING HEART.` · `TESTIMONY — A WITNESS.` · `MARTYS — WITNESS, THEN MARTYR.`

segments.voice: Three breaths with the bell. On the first, think of one thing that really happened to you, something that changed you even a little. On the second, say to yourself, in one plain sentence, what happened. On the third, let it rest. A witness doesn't add anything.
Testimony. From the Greek for witness: here's what I saw happen. Fifth word.
Your line: your story is a witness. A quiet one counts as much as a bonfire one. Five days in.

howItsDone: Many evangelical churches, youth groups and camps invite people to share a testimony, the story of how they came to faith, aloud; many Christians also keep a daily quiet time of Bible reading and prayer, often in the morning.

myth: the word martyr first meant witness
Greek martys, a witness. it came to mean someone who died for what they witnessed.
quiet time is a phrase from the Bible
it's a church phrase, modeled on Jesus going off early to a solitary place to pray.
a testimony has to be dramatic
it's a witness statement: what happened to you. a quiet one counts.

fork.setup: after a long day of crowds, one Gospel shows Jesus the next morning. what does he do?
options: gets up a great while before day and goes off alone to pray.
starts teaching the crowd right away.
fork.reveal: a great while before day, he went off to a solitary place to pray. that's the model behind a quiet time.

original.note: Greek: testimony, witness. from martys, a witness, the root of English martyr.

trapdoor: what you thought: a dramatic conversion speech by the bonfire.
what it means: a witness statement: here's what I saw happen.
what a scholar hears: martys was a legal witness; by the second century it named those who died for their witness (the Martyrdom of Polycarp), hence English martyr.

story.title: the woman who left her water jar
story.text: A woman walks to the town well at noon, in the heat of the day. A tired stranger sitting there, a Jewish man, asks her for a drink, which surprises her: Jews and Samaritans kept apart. They talk, and he tells her things about her own life he shouldn't know. She leaves her water jar right there and runs back into town: come and see a man who told me everything I ever did. The story says many in that town believed because of what she testified.

wrong.myth: a testimony has to be a dramatic before-and-after story.
wrong.truth: the word means a witness statement: what you saw happen. a short, quiet one is still a testimony.

notes: New lesson (2026-10-06), written from the audience research: 'Christianese decoded' (top-20 moment 8, proposed day 5). The strand word is testimony, the phrase with the most behind it.
Quiet time tied to Mark 1:35 as 'a model'; on fire tied to Luke 24:32 as 'it echoes'. Neither claims the phrase comes from the verse. Confirm.
martys → martyr: by the mid-second century martys names those who died for their witness (Martyrdom of Polycarp); Acts 22:20 (Stephen 'thy martyr', KJV) shows the turn. Confirm wording.
Sensitive: the research notes some people felt pressured to share a testimony aloud. The script says plenty keep theirs private, and the think card makes passing an honest option. Read for tone.
Story card: the woman at the well (John 4:39, 'which testified'). 'At noon, in the heat of the day' renders 'the sixth hour'; no claim about why she came alone.
